# ROUND-4 fixture: the ADVISORY twin of python-pip-audit-blocking.
#
# The blocking path (a `.pip-audit-ignore` file present) had a fixture; the
# advisory path - the one every Python consumer gets by DEFAULT, with no
# opt-in file - had none. So "pip-audit found something real, warn but do
# not block" had never once executed in this repo's CI, and the branch that
# distinguishes it from "pip-audit itself crashed" was unproven in exactly
# the way the blocking path's turned out to be wrong (see
# python-pip-audit-blocking/requirements.txt).
#
# Deliberately NO .pip-audit-ignore in this directory: its absence is what
# routes this fixture to the advisory step (has_pip_audit_ignore == 'false').
#
# Same vulnerable pin as the blocking fixture, and for the same reason:
# Jinja2 is not a dependency, direct or transitive, of any of the reusable
# workflow's five pinned tools (ruff/pytest/mypy/bandit/pip-audit), so no
# tool's own version floor can ever conflict with this pin and crash the
# resolve before the CVEs are looked up - the exact bug that left the
# blocking fixture never reaching its intended branch.
#
# Expected result: this job PASSES (advisory means advisory), and its assert
# job greps its real log for the rendered
# "##[warning]pip-audit reported findings (advisory step, not blocking)"
# annotation - because a job that passes proves nothing on its own here. It
# also asserts the crash annotation is ABSENT, so a future resolver conflict
# cannot masquerade as advisory coverage.
Jinja2==3.1.4
